To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the desorption energies of linear alkanes on single-crystalline surfaces scale linearly in the length of the alkane chain, and that the intercepts of the linear and cyclic chains are similar on a given surface.

for sets of short linear alkanes and sets of cyclic alkanes, the desorption energies scale with the number of carbons in the molecule, N, with the form ΔE(N)=ΔE+ΔECH·N, where ΔECH is the segmental contribution to desorption energy and ΔE is the intercept.

the desorption energies of short linear and short cyclic alkanes from surfaces scale linearly in the chain length, with the form ΔE(N)=ΔE+ΔECH·N, and that the intercept, ΔE, is similar for the linear and the cyclic alkanes, ruling out the possibility that the intercept arises from endgroup or polarizability effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the scaling of the desorption energies of linear, cyclic and branched alkanes on single crystalline surfaces as a function of chain length.
the desorption energies of short linear and ring alkanes from the Cu(111) and Pt(111) surfaces.
the desorption of linear and cyclic hydrocarbon molecules from metal surfaces.

the origin of the intercept, ΔE, remains an open question.

the desorption energies of linear alkanes on Cu and Pt are similar in magnitude to those of cyclic alkanes.
